updates.name: Lihini I. Aluwihare
updates.bio: Chemical oceanographer and Professor in the Geosciences Research Division at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego, where she has worked since 2000. She traces carbon and nitrogen cycling in aquatic systems with isotope tracers and molecular characterization of organic matter, including microbial metabolite interactions and anthropogenic organic compounds in coastal waters.
updates.research_interests: production, transformation and removal of aquatic organic matter; dissolved organic matter in the ocean biological carbon pump; nitrogen cycling in the coastal California Current Ecosystem; dissolved molecules mediating microbe-microbe interactions; halogenated organic compounds in coastal environments; LC ESI MS and GC TOF MS characterization of organic matter; compound-specific stable and radioisotope measurements
updates.current_title: Professor, Geosciences Research Division (Marine Chemistry and Geochemistry)

updates.name: Lisa A. Levin
updates.bio: Marine ecologist and Distinguished Professor Emerita at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego, and director of its Center for Marine Biodiversity and Conservation from 2011 to 2017. She studies deep-sea and coastal benthic ecosystems, especially methane seeps and oxygen minimum zones, climate-driven deoxygenation, and deep-ocean policy; she co-founded the Deep-Ocean Stewardship Initiative.
updates.research_interests: biodiversity, function and ecosystem services of deep-sea methane seeps and oxygen minimum zones; deep-sea science for international policy; climate change, ocean deoxygenation and acidification on continental margins; wetland invasion, restoration and water re-use; connectivity in coastal ecosystems; deep-sea conservation and sustainability; invertebrate life histories, dispersal and demography

updates.name: Louis A. Sass III
updates.bio: Physical scientist at the USGS Alaska Science Center since 2012 and lead of the Alaska part of the USGS Benchmark Glacier Project, which includes Gulkana and Wolverine glaciers. He measures glacier mass change, the physical processes and feedbacks behind it, and how glaciers shape runoff and downstream ecosystems. MS in environmental science, Alaska Pacific University.
updates.research_interests: glacier mass balance; physical processes of glacier mass balance; feedback mechanisms on glacier mass balance; glacier influences on streamflow
updates.current_affiliation: U.S. Geological Survey, Alaska Science Center

updates.name: M. Alisa Mast
updates.bio: Research hydrologist with the USGS Colorado Water Science Center in Denver. Projects and products on her USGS profile include water-quality sampling at Hydrologic Benchmark Network stations in the western U.S., wet nitrogen deposition tracking at Rocky Mountain National Park, ion elution from melting snowpacks, and water chemistry of legacy mine lands in central Colorado headwaters.
updates.research_interests: Hydrologic Benchmark Network water quality; wet atmospheric nitrogen deposition (Rocky Mountain National Park); preferential elution of ionic solutes from melting snowpacks; legacy mine-land water chemistry in Colorado headwaters
updates.current_affiliation: U.S. Geological Survey, Colorado Water Science Center

updates.name: M. Jake Vander Zanden
updates.bio: Director of the UW-Madison Center for Limnology, whose field sites include Trout Lake Station, and Professor of Biology holding the Wayland Noland Distinguished Chair. His lab applies food-web approaches to freshwater ecosystems and their threats, using long-term data, whole-lake experiments, stable isotopes and modelling to study invasive species, benthic production and walleye declines.
updates.research_interests: freshwater food webs; spread and impacts of aquatic invasive species; benthic primary production and nearshore habitats in lakes; inland walleye fishery declines and food-web-based lake restoration; stable isotope analysis; whole-lake experiments and long-term studies

updates.name: M. Syndonia Bret-Harte
updates.bio: Plant community and ecosystem ecologist and professor at the University of Alaska Fairbanks, affiliated with the Institute of Arctic Biology and the Department of Biology and Wildlife. She examines how a changing climate shifts Arctic plant community composition and nutrient cycling, and serves as science director and principal investigator for Toolik Field Station.
updates.research_interests: climate change effects on Arctic vegetation composition; Arctic nutrient cycling; plant community and ecosystem ecology

updates.name: Margaret Leinen
updates.bio: Oceanographer and Professor at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego, who led Scripps as its eleventh director from October 2013 to September 2025 while serving as UC San Diego Vice Chancellor for Marine Sciences. Her research uses ocean sediments to reconstruct past ocean, climate and biogeochemical cycles. Previously NSF Assistant Director for Geosciences and AGU president.
updates.research_interests: paleoceanography and paleoclimatology; ocean biogeochemical cycling; global change impacts on the ocean; ocean observing systems; climate engineering; ocean and climate policy
